intended_object: The determinant det(m_{i+j}) for 0 ≤ i, j < h of a sequence of polynomials m_j ∈ K[X], i.e. the leading h×h Hankel determinant. It serves as the common denominator in a Cramer's-rule formula for the coefficients of a "generic moment support polynomial" in the GapCVP reduction proof. I inferred this from the body, the name and how the library uses it; the docstring only says "GapCVP reduction support."
explanation:
The body is `leadingHankelDet moments h`, a private helper equal to `(Matrix.of fun i j => moments (i + j) : Matrix (Fin h) (Fin h) K[X]).det`. It correctly computes the h×h Hankel determinant of the moment sequence.

The definition itself is a public alias of that private helper. It exists to name the "denominator" used inside the reduction proof:
- `genericHankelCoefficient` is defined as numerator / denominator in `RatFunc K`.
- It is the leading coefficient of `clearedGenericMomentSupportPolynomial`.
- Its degree bounds and nonvanishing at "good points" feed a counting argument.

The docstring gives no mathematical meaning ("GapCVP reduction support"), and both the name and the uses tie it to one step of one proof. It does not present it as a standalone notion. So I classify it as a proof-internal technical device.

Two caveats. If it were read as "the Hankel determinant" in general, it would arguably be too narrow, because nothing in the body needs `K[X]` with `K` a field: the construction makes sense for any sequence in any commutative ring. Mathlib has no Hankel-matrix or Hankel-determinant definition (grep for "Hankel" finds nothing). Neither caveat changes the classification: in this library the definition is an auxiliary denominator for this proof, and as such it is computed correctly.
